data.name: Shyamala
data.gender_notes: Shyamala is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit 'shyama' meaning 'dark' or 'night'. Often associated with Goddess Kali or Durga. The name Shyamala carries the meaning “Dark Night” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Shyamala usually hope their child will grow to embody dark night and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine feminine power and protection.
data.etymology: Shyamala belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dark Night.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shyamala total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Shyamala carries cultural significance as it is commonly used in the Hindu tradition. It is reminiscent of the divine feminine, linked to powerful goddesses such as Kali and Durga, who embody strength, protection, and the cycle of life and death.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, the name Shyamala holds deep symbolism representing the feminine divine, the eternal force of darkness and night that offers nourishment and renewal. It serves as a reminder of the transformative power of adversity and the inner strength that comes from embracing the dark aspects of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Shyamala: Goddess of Coolness and Compassion. Embodiment of tranquility and nurturing motherly love, bestowing grace and inner peace.

vedic_reference.note: From Rigveda, Shyamala is a name of the goddess Durga, also known as Parvati.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The name Shyamala is mentioned in the Mahabharata as a queen of the kingdom of Hastinapura. The name Shyamala carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name is associated with the goddess Lakshmi and is considered auspicious in Hindu mythology.

trends: increasing popularity in India as a given name
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Shyamala remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: Maya Shyamala from Bali, Indonesia embodies the meaning of Shyamala - "Dark Night". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
